dedupe_keys.name: global waste sector dataset 1990 2050 scenario projections of generation emissions and socioeconomic drivers

description: This data set gives harmonised national time series of municipal solid waste generation and waste-sector greenhouse gas emissions for 43 countries, with the population and income that drive them, from 1990 to 2020 and projected to 2050. For each country and year it records population, GDP per capita at purchasing power parity, waste generated in tonnes, and carbon dioxide, methane (also expressed with the GWP* metric for short-lived climate effects) and nitrous oxide emissions from waste. The producers are Zheng Xuan Hoy, Kok Sin Woon and colleagues at Xiamen University Malaysia, the National University of Singapore, the University of Oxford and Sookmyung Women's University, published as a data article in Frontiers in Environmental Science in January 2026. Forecasts come from an ensemble of fixed-effects regressions and artificial neural networks. Data are free as a FAIR2 data package with metadata and an interactive portal under the Open Data Commons Attribution Licence. Caveats: only national aggregates, only 43 countries, and projections carry scenario and model uncertainty that the files do not resolve by waste stream or treatment route. Simulation uses: future waste generation to size collection, landfill and treatment capacity, and emissions pathways for climate scenarios of the waste sector. Related records: the What a Waste database (data-what-a-waste-global-database) provides city-level baselines.
